summary_md: **Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Papers ([@CSVisionPapers](https://x.com/CSVisionPapers/status/2116094008900391254))** shares *PhysCreator* ([arXiv 2610.34473](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34473)) by Zheng et al., a feed-forward framework that generates simulation-ready 3D assets from images with spatially varying physical properties in a voxel-aligned latent space.

referenced_urls.title: PhysCreator: Creating Physically-Attributed 3D Assets at Will

relevance: Physics-aware 3D asset generation for simulation and animation.

media.ocr_text: Significant advancements in 3D asset creation have enabled high-fidelity 3D generation from images. However, most existing representations remain inherently static, lacking the ability to model physically plausible behaviors under dynamic interactions. We present PhysCreator, a unified framework that directly generates simulation-ready 3D representations with spatially varying physical properties from images. Unlike prior approaches that treat physical attributes as simple post-hoc predictions or rely on expensive per-instance optimization, we reformulate physical property estimation within a unified 3D representation learning framework. We introduce a voxel-aligned latent space by lifting image observations into a spatially structured 3D representation, in which geometry, appearance, and physical properties are jointly modeled and inferred in a feed-forward manner.
